rules.title: Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy
rules.requirement: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies in residential rental property.
rules.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy; short-term residential occupancy; deed- or regulatory-restricted affordable housing; housing with government affordable housing subsidies (excluding Section 8); mobilehomes subject to the Mobilehome Residency Law; nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care facilities, licensed residential care facilities for the elderly, adult residential facilities, or non-profit transitional housing; school dormitories; properties where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with a resident landlord; landlord-occupied single-family residences renting no more than two bedrooms or two ADUs/JADUs; properties with two separate dwelling units where the landlord resides in one; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome); and separately alienable rental properties not owned by a REIT, corporation, or corporate LLC where required exemption notice is provided.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this 
Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.

rules.title: Owner or Relative Move-In Just Cause Requirements
rules.requirement: An owner acting in good faith may terminate a tenancy to recover possession to occupy the property for the owner or their qualified relative for a minimum of 12 continuous months as a primary residence. For leases entered into on or after June 24, 2023, this applies only if the tenant agrees in writing or the lease expressly allows it; it does not apply if the intended occupant already occupies a unit on the property or a vacancy of a similar unit already exists.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies in residential rental property.
rules.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy; short-term residential occupancy; deed- or regulatory-restricted affordable housing; housing with government affordable housing subsidies (excluding Section 8); mobilehomes subject to the Mobilehome Residency Law; nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care facilities, licensed residential care facilities for the elderly, adult residential facilities, or non-profit transitional housing; school dormitories; properties where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with a resident landlord; landlord-occupied single-family residences renting no more than two bedrooms or two ADUs/JADUs; properties with two separate dwelling units where the landlord resides in one; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome); and separately alienable rental properties not owned by a REIT, corporation, or corporate LLC where required exemption notice is provided.
rules.quoted_span:
(1) The owner seeks to recover possession to occupy the residential rental 
property for the owner or their spouse, domestic partner, child (by 
blood or adoption), grandchild (by blood or adoption), parent, or 
grandparent for a minimum of 12 continuous months as that person’s 
primary residence. 
(A) For leases entered into on or after June 24, 2023, section 
98.0704(b)(1) shall apply only if the tenant agrees to the 
termination in writing or if the lease expressly allows the 
owner to terminate the lease if the owner unilaterally decides 
to occupy the residential rental property for the owner or their 
spouse, domestic partner, child (by blood or adoption), 
grandchild (by blood or adoption), parent, or grandparent. 
(B) For tenancies in effect prior to June 24, 2023, the addition of a 
provision allowing the owner to terminate the lease as 
described in section 98.0704(b)(1) to a new lease, renewed 
lease, or fixed-term lease constitutes a substantially similar 
provision for the purposes of section 98.0704(a)(5). 
(C) Section 98.0704(b)(1) does not apply if the intended occupant 
occupies a rental unit on the property or if a vacancy of a 
similar unit already exists at the property.

rules.title: Owner Move-In Notice Contents and Proof of Relationship
rules.requirement: The written termination notice for an owner or relative move-in must contain the name or names and relationship to the owner of the intended occupant, and notice that the tenant may request proof that the intended occupant is the owner or related to the owner; the owner must provide such proof upon request.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies terminated for owner or relative move-in.
rules.quoted_span:

section 98.0704(b)(1) shall contain the name or names and 
relationship to the owner of the intended occupant. In addition, 
the written notice shall include notification that the tenant may 
request proof that the intended occupant is the owner or related 
to the owner. The owner shall provide tenant the proof upon 
request, which may include an operating agreement and other 
non-public documents.

rules.title: Owner Move-In Failure to Occupy Remedies
rules.requirement: If the intended occupant does not occupy the property within 90 days after the tenant vacates or for at least 12 continuous months, the owner must offer the property back to the vacated tenant at the same rent and lease terms and reimburse the tenant for reasonable moving expenses incurred in excess of any relocation assistance paid.
rules.coverage_conditions: Properties where tenancy was terminated for owner or relative move-in.
rules.exemptions: If the intended occupant moves in within 90 days but dies before occupying for 12 continuous months, it is not considered a failure to comply or a violation.
rules.quoted_span:
(E) Section 98.0704(b)(1) applies only if the intended occupant 
moves into the residential rental property within 90 days after 
the tenant vacates and occupies the residential rental property 
for at least 12 continuous months. 
(F) If the intended occupant does not occupy the residential rental 
property within 90 days after the tenant vacates or does not 
occupy the residential rental property for at least 12 
continuous months, the owner shall offer the residential rental 
property to the tenant who vacated it at the same rent and lease 
terms in effect at the time the tenant vacated and shall 
reimburse the tenant for reasonable moving expenses incurred 
in excess of any relocation assistance that was paid to the 
tenant in connection with the written notice terminating the 
tenancy.

rules.title: Government Order to Vacate Just Cause Requirements
rules.requirement: A landlord may terminate a tenancy for no-fault just cause to comply with an order issued by a government agency or court relating to habitability requiring vacating for at least 30 days, an order to vacate, or a local ordinance requiring vacating. If a government agency or court determines the tenant is at fault for the triggering condition, the tenant is not entitled to relocation assistance.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies in residential rental property.
rules.exemptions: An order relating to habitability that requires vacating for fewer than 30 days is not grounds to terminate a tenancy for just cause.
rules.quoted_span:
(3) The landlord seeks to recover possession to comply with any of the 
following:  
(A) an order issued by a government agency or court relating to 
habitability that requires vacating the residential rental 
property for at least 30 days. An order issued by a government 
agency or court relating to habitability that requires vacating 
the residential rental property for fewer than 30 days is not 
grounds to terminate a tenancy for just cause and a landlord 
may be required by applicable state or federal law to provide

(B) an order issued by a government agency or court to vacate the

(C) a local ordinance that requires vacating the residential rental

under section 98.0704(b)(3), the tenant shall not be entitled to any 
relocation assistance provided in section 98.0706(c).

rules.title: Demolition or Substantial Remodel Permit Requirements
rules.requirement: If permits are required for demolition or substantial remodel, the landlord must post a copy of the permit application at the property within three business days of submittal, and secure all necessary permits prior to issuing the written notice of termination.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property being demolished or substantially remodeled requiring permits.
rules.quoted_span:
(C) If permits are required for the demolition or substantial 
remodel of the residential rental property, landlord shall:  
(i) post at the residential rental property a copy of the 
application for the necessary permits within three 
business days of submittal of the application; and  
(ii) secure permits necessary for the demolition or 
substantial remodel of the residential rental property 
prior to issuing the written notice required in section 
98.0704(b)(4)(D).

rules.title: Mandatory Notice of Residential Tenant Protections
rules.requirement: A landlord must provide written notice in at least 12-point font stating that California law limits rent increases, local law requires a statement of cause for termination, and seniors or disabled tenants may be entitled to additional protections, accompanied by a copy of the Tenant Protection Guide.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property subject to Division 7.
rules.quoted_span:
(a) A landlord of residential rental property subject to this Division shall provide 
written notice in no less than 12-point font to the tenant, and in a manner that 
complies with California Civil Code section 1632, as may be amended, that 
states as follows: 
California law limits the amount your rent can be increased. See 
California Civil Code section 1947.12 for more information. Local law 
also provides that a landlord shall provide a statement of cause in any 
notice to terminate a tenancy. In some circumstances, tenants who are 
seniors (62 years or older) or disabled may be entitled to additional 
tenant protections. See Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 7 of the San 
Diego Municipal Code for more information. 
 
(b) A landlord of residential rental property subject to this Division shall include 
a copy of the Tenant Protection Guide with the written notice required by 
section 98.0705(a).

rules.title: Delivery Timing for Tenant Protections Notice and Guide
rules.requirement: For tenancies existing before June 24, 2023, the required disclosure and Tenant Protection Guide must be provided directly or as a lease addendum within 90 days of June 24, 2023; for tenancies commencing or renewed on or after June 24, 2023, they must be included in the lease or provided as a signed written notice at lease signing.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies in residential rental property subject to Division 7.
rules.quoted_span:
(c) For a tenancy in a residential rental property subject to this Division existing 
before June 24, 2023, the notice required by section 98.0705(a) and the 
Tenant Protection Guide required by section 98.0705(b) shall be provided to

(d) For a tenancy in a residential rental property subject to this Division 
commencing or renewed on or after June 24, 2023, the notice required by 
section 98.0705(a) and the Tenant Protection Guide required by 
section 98.0705(b) shall be included in the lease, or as a written notice signed 
by the tenant at the time the lease is signed, with a copy provided to the 
tenant.

rules.title: Opportunity to Cure Curable At-Fault Violations
rules.requirement: Before issuing a termination notice for a curable at-fault lease violation, the landlord must give written notice describing the violation and an opportunity to cure; if not cured within the notice period, the landlord may terminate without another cure opportunity by serving a three-day notice to quit.
rules.coverage_conditions: At-fault terminations for curable lease violations.
rules.quoted_span:
(1) Notice to Tenant. Before a landlord issues a notice to terminate a 
tenancy for at-fault just cause that is a curable lease violation, the 
landlord shall first give written notice of the violation including a 
description of the violation and an opportunity to cure the violation 
under California Code of Civil Procedure section 1161(3), as may be 
amended. If the violation is not cured within the time period in the 
notice, the landlord may terminate the tenancy without another 
opportunity to cure by serving a three-day notice to quit.

rules.title: Notice to Commission of At-Fault Termination
rules.requirement: A landlord must provide written notice to the Commission of an at-fault termination no later than three business days after providing the required notice to the tenant, once the submission portal is established.
rules.coverage_conditions: At-fault just cause terminations of tenancy.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply until 30 days after the Commission establishes a submission portal and provides public notice.
rules.quoted_span:
(2) Notice to Commission. The landlord shall provide written notice to the 
Commission of the at-fault just cause termination of tenancy under 
section 98.0704(a) no later than three business days after the date the 
landlord provided the required notice to tenant. Section 98.0706(a)(2) 
shall not apply until 30 days after the Commission establishes a 
submission portal and provides the public notice of its creation.

rules.title: Notice to Commission of No-Fault Termination
rules.requirement: The landlord must provide written notice to the Commission of a no-fault just cause termination no later than three business days after providing the required notice to the tenant, once the submission portal is established.
rules.coverage_conditions: No-fault just cause terminations of tenancy.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply until 30 days after the Commission establishes a submission portal and provides public notice.
rules.quoted_span:
(2) Notice to Commission. The landlord shall provide written notice to the 
Commission of the no-fault just cause termination of tenancy under 
section 98.0704(b) no later than three business days after the date the 
landlord provided the required notice to tenant. Section 98.0706(b)(2) 
shall not apply until 30 days after the Commission establishes a

rules.title: Relocation Assistance Independent from Security Deposit Return
rules.requirement: Required relocation assistance does not relieve the landlord's obligation to return any deposit or security amounts owed to the tenant and must be provided in addition to the return of any deposit or security.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants receiving relocation assistance under Division 7.
rules.quoted_span:
(3) The relocation assistance required by this Division shall not relieve the 
landlord’s obligation to, and shall be in addition to, the return of any 
deposit or security amounts owed to the tenant.

rules.title: Relocation Assistance Credit Against Other Laws
rules.requirement: Any relocation assistance required by this Division must be credited against any other relocation assistance required by any federal, state, or other local law.
rules.coverage_conditions: Relocation assistance provided under Division 7.
rules.interaction: Credited against any other relocation assistance required by any federal, state, or other local law.
rules.quoted_span:
(4) Any relocation assistance required by this Division shall be credited 
against any other relocation assistance required by any federal, state, 
or other local law.

rules.title: Displaced Tenant Right of First Offer to Re-Rent Within Five Years
rules.requirement: If a property is offered for rent within five years of eviction under owner move-in, government order, or demolition/remodel, the landlord must first offer to lease the property in writing to the displaced tenant (if the tenant gave timely notice and contact information); the landlord may screen using industry accepted methods with criteria communicated in the offer, and the tenant has 30 days to accept.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property re-offered for rent within five years of eviction under sections 98.0704(b)(1), (3), or (4).
rules.quoted_span:
If a residential rental property is offered for rent or lease for residential 
purposes within five years of the date the tenant was evicted under 
sections 98.0704(b)(1), (3), or (4), landlord shall first offer to lease the 
residential rental property in writing to the tenant displaced from that unit by 
the no-fault just cause termination if the tenant:   
(1) advised the landlord in writing within 30 days of the termination 
notice of the tenant’s desire to receive an offer to renew the tenancy; 
and  
(2) provided the landlord a mailing address or email address for the 
landlord to send the offer, including any change of mailing address or 
email address.  
The landlord shall have the right to screen the tenant using industry accepted 
methods and shall communicate the minimum screening criteria in the written 
offer for the new tenancy. The tenant shall have 30 days from the date of 
receipt of the offer to accept.

rules.title: Strict Compliance with Termination Requirements
rules.requirement: A landlord's failure to strictly comply with section 98.0706 renders void any notice of termination required by the section.
rules.coverage_conditions: Notices of termination required under § 98.0706.
rules.quoted_span:
(e) In addition to other remedies applicable to landlord’s failure to comply with 
this Division, a landlord's failure to strictly comply with section 98.0706 shall 
render void any notice of termination required by section 98.0706.

rules.title: Buyout Disclosure Recordkeeping and Delivery
rules.requirement: The landlord must provide each tenant an executed copy of the buyout disclosure form within three days of execution and retain a copy and record of the delivery date for five years.
rules.coverage_conditions: Buyout offer disclosures executed under § 98.0707.
rules.quoted_span:
(b) The landlord shall provide each tenant a fully executed copy of the disclosure 
form within three days of its execution and retain a copy of each signed 
disclosure form for five years, along with a record of the date the landlord 
provided the disclosure to each tenant.

rules.title: Minimum Compensation for Buyout Agreements
rules.requirement: Buyout agreements must be for an amount greater than the amount of relocation assistance available under section 98.0706(c); any buyout agreement for less than the relocation assistance owed is void.
rules.coverage_conditions: Buyout agreements for residential rental property.
rules.quoted_span:
(d) Void Buyout Agreements. Buyout agreements must be for an amount that is 
greater than the amount of relocation assistance available to the tenant in 
section 98.0706(c). A buyout agreement for less than the amount of relocation 
assistance owed to the tenant violates this Division and is void.

rules.title: Non-Waivability of Buyout Agreement Rights
rules.requirement: The provisions governing buyout agreements cannot be waived, and any agreement term purporting to waive or limit tenant rights under section 98.0707 is contrary to public policy, unenforceable, and void.
rules.coverage_conditions: Buyout agreements, leases, contracts, or other agreements concerning residential rental property.
rules.quoted_span:
(e) No Waiver. The provisions of section 98.0707 may not be waived by a buyout 
agreement. Any term of a buyout agreement, lease, contract, or other 
agreement which purports to waive or limit a tenant's rights under 
section 98.0707 is contrary to public policy, unenforceable, and void.

rules.title: Retaliation Prohibited
rules.requirement: A landlord shall not retaliate against a tenant for exercising any right provided by Division 7 or seeking its enforcement.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants in residential rental properties.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord shall not retaliate against a tenant for exercising any right provided by 
this Division or seeking the enforcement of this Division.

rules.title: Treble Damages for Wrongful Eviction
rules.requirement: Any attempt or actual recovery of possession of residential rental property in violation of this Division renders the landlord liable to the tenant in a civil action for wrongful eviction damages of not less than three times actual economic damages.
rules.coverage_conditions: Violations involving attempt or actual recovery of possession.
rules.quoted_span:
(d) Any attempt by a landlord to recover possession of a residential rental 
property or any actual recovery of possession of a residential rental property 
in violation of this Division shall render the landlord liable to the tenant in a 
civil action for wrongful eviction for damages of not less than three times the 
actual economic damages.

rules.title: Treble Damages for Failure to Provide Relocation Assistance
rules.requirement: Any landlord who fails to provide required relocation assistance is liable to the tenant in a civil action for not less than three times the required relocation assistance and actual economic damages.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords failing to provide relocation assistance under § 98.0706(c).
rules.quoted_span:
(e) Any landlord who fails to provide relocation assistance as required by 
section 98.0706(c) shall be liable to the tenant in a civil action for not less 
than three times the required relocation assistance and actual economic 
damages.

rules.title: Attorney's Fees for Material Violations
rules.requirement: In the court's discretion, a landlord who attempts to recover possession in material violation of this Division is liable to the tenant in a civil action for reasonable attorney's fees and costs.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlord attempts to recover possession in material violation of Division 7.
rules.quoted_span:
(f) In the court's discretion, a landlord who attempts to recover possession of a 
residential rental property in material violation of this Division shall be liable 
to the tenant in a civil action for reasonable attorney’s fees and costs.

rules.title: Failure to Comply Renders Notice of Termination Void
rules.requirement: In addition to other remedies, a landlord's failure to comply with any provision of this Division renders void any notice of termination required by the Division.
rules.coverage_conditions: Notices of termination required under Division 7.
rules.quoted_span:
In addition to other remedies applicable to landlord’s failure to comply with this 
Division, a landlord’s failure to comply with any provision of this Division shall 
render void any notice of termination required by this Division.
